title: Is Brutal Honesty a Virtue or an Alibi?
script: Rangga: [provocative] You always frame your bluntness as integrity, Dinda, but I sometimes wonder whether it's really just cruelty that's found itself a respectable vocabulary.
Dinda: [amused] And you always frame your tact as kindness, Rangga, though half the time it looks to me like cowardice wearing a more presentable coat.
Rangga: [firm] There's a difference between cowardice and consideration. I withheld my opinion of Bram's business plan because the timing would have crushed him unnecessarily.
Dinda: [pointed] Or you withheld it because disagreeing felt uncomfortable, and you dressed that discomfort up afterward as concern for his feelings.
Rangga: [defensive] That's an ungenerous reading of a decision that, as far as I can tell, spared someone a devastating conversation he wasn't ready to have.
Dinda: [thoughtful] Maybe. But he built three more months of momentum on a plan you privately considered doomed, and that cost him more than honesty would have.
Rangga: [conceding] I hadn't weighed it that way, admittedly. I suppose I measured the discomfort of the conversation rather than the cost of postponing it.
Dinda: [gently] Honesty isn't a bluntness contest, though, whatever you seem to assume about how I practice it. I choose my timing as carefully as you choose your silence.
Rangga: [curious] So where's the line between tact that protects someone and tact that simply protects you from an uncomfortable ten minutes?
Dinda: [reflective] I ask myself whether my silence serves the other person or only my own comfort. If it's the latter, I've just repackaged cowardice.
Rangga: [honestly] By that measure, my silence with Bram served me more than it served him, however reasonable it felt at the time.
Dinda: [warmly] That's a harder admission than most people manage.
Rangga: [wry] Don't get used to it. I still think you could deliver a hard truth with slightly more cushioning than you generally bother with.
Dinda: [smiling] And I still think you could deliver an easy truth without waiting for the perfect, ever-elusive moment to arrive.
Rangga: [amused] Perhaps we should each borrow a little from the other, then, before one of us does real damage with our preferred approach.
Dinda: [warmly] Agreed. Starting with Bram, who deserves an honest conversation from at least one of us, sooner rather than later.

quiz.question: What does Rangga accuse Dinda of when it comes to her bluntness?
options: Being too diplomatic
Dressing up cruelty in a respectable vocabulary
Never sharing her real opinion
Only being honest with strangers
quiz.explanation: Rangga suggests her bluntness might really just be cruelty that has found a respectable vocabulary.

quiz.question: Why did Rangga withhold his real opinion of Bram's business plan?
options: He agreed with the plan completely
He believed the timing would have crushed Bram unnecessarily
He hadn't reviewed the plan yet
Bram never asked for his opinion
quiz.explanation: Rangga says he withheld his opinion because the timing would have crushed Bram unnecessarily.

quiz.question: What cost does Dinda point out from Rangga's silence?
options: Bram lost his job
Bram built three more months of momentum on a plan Rangga privately considered doomed
Bram found out from someone else immediately
There was no real cost
quiz.explanation: Dinda points out that Bram built three more months of momentum on a plan Rangga privately considered doomed.

quiz.question: How does Dinda test whether her own silence is justified?
options: She never questions her silence
She asks whether the silence serves the other person or only her own comfort
She asks a third party to decide
She assumes silence is always the safest choice
quiz.explanation: She asks herself whether her silence serves the other person or only her own comfort, calling the latter repackaged cowardice.

quiz.question: What do Rangga and Dinda agree to do by the end of the conversation?
options: Avoid Bram entirely
Each borrow a little from the other's approach, starting with an honest conversation with Bram
End their friendship over the disagreement
Let Bram figure things out alone
quiz.explanation: They agree to borrow from each other's approach and that Bram deserves an honest conversation from at least one of them soon.
